Microsoft's Incident Report for PennO365
Following is a data extract from the PennO365 administrative console of incident reports sent by Microsoft within the last 30 days. We pull out incidents that are relevant to the current PennO365 service offerings and we refresh this data every 15 minutes. Note that incidents related to PennO365 administrative functions are not shown in this list. Additionally you can check Microsoft's status page for current service status messages. This extract was generated Sat Nov 14 00:50:01 2026 EST.
MO1550821 - Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services
Status:	serviceRestored
Start Time:	Thu Nov 12 10:05:00 2026 UTC (Thu Nov 12 05:05:00 2026 EST)
End Time:	Fri Nov 13 04:10:00 2026 UTC (Thu Nov 12 23:10:00 2026 EST)
Service:	Microsoft 365 suite
Feature Group:	Portal
Classification:	incident
Last Updated:	Sat Nov 14 04:17:52 2026 UTC (Fri Nov 13 23:17:52 2026 EST)
Root Cause:	N/A
Next Update:	N/A
collapse section Details

Time:	Sat Nov 14 04:17:52 2026 UTC (Fri Nov 13 23:17:52 2026 EST)
Description:	Title: Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services
User impact: Users may have been unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services.
Final status: This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents.
The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.
Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.
More info: Features of the Microsoft 365 services below that interact with Exchange Online and email services were impacted. Elements of those services that do not depend on interaction with Exchange Online remained functional.
- Exchange Online: Users may be unable to access their mailbox using Outlook on the web, Outlook desktop (MAPI), Exchange ActiveSync (EAS), or REST-based connections, and email delivery may be delayed.
- Microsoft 365 admin center: Admins may be unable to load some admin center pages.
- Microsoft 365 apps: Users may be unable to view their recently used files.
- Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center: Multiple services including Cloud Update, Cloud Policy, and Inventory are affected.
- Microsoft 365 Education: Features including Assignments, Reading Progress, and Speaker Progress may be impacted.
- Microsoft Copilot 365: Users may be unable to load Copilot Chat or receive responses in the web and desktop apps, and Copilot experiences may be unable to access work data such as email, calendar, and files.
- Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Some Defender for Office 365 experiences that rely on Purview DLP/Information Protection signals may experience delays or failures in policy evaluation and governance action enforcement. Admins/SOCs may experience delays or failures when accessing NHI features that rely on Data Classification Sensitivity Labels, including Tenant Metrics, Policy, and Data Usage, across the Identity, OAuth, and App Governance pages in the Security portal on Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
- Microsoft Defender XDR: Users may be unable to load Microsoft Defender portal pages or solution tabs.
- Microsoft Fabric: Users may encounter failures when exporting reports with sensitivity labels to PDF or PowerPoint, when updating artifacts with sensitivity labels, or opening pbix with sensitivity label in Power BI Desktop. As a workaround, users can remove the sensitivity label from the affected item to complete the operation, if their organization's data protection policies allow it.
- Microsoft Graph: API requests that access Exchange Online data, such as mail, calendar, and contacts, may time out and prevent users from managing Teams, Channels, Membership, Apps management and send activity notifications using Graph API.
- Microsoft Intune: Scenarios including device enrollment, device check-in, and device compliance policies may have been intermittently impacted.
- Microsoft Planner: Users are experiencing Plan and Task operation reliability issues.
- Microsoft Power Apps: Users may be intermittently unable to sign-in to the Power Apps or Field Service mobile apps. Affected users may be able to utilize Power Apps or Field Service on the web as a way to circumvent impact, and users who are already signed in can potentially avoid impact by not signing out, clearing app data, or reinstalling while the issue is ongoing. Microsoft Power Apps and Microsoft Power Automate Flows, apps, data refreshes and connectors that rely on Microsoft Graph data were intermittently failing.
- Microsoft Purview: Multiple Purview services including Authorization, auto-labeling, Data Loss Prevention (DLP) across Microsoft 365 services, Communication Compliance, Information Protection label and auto-labeling policies, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Data Classification are impacted, and users may be unable to open or load Microsoft Purview portal pages or protected content. Audit searches, protected content creation, eDiscovery tasks such as search and export, Data Classification and On Demand Scan features may also be impacted.
- Microsoft Teams: Most of the core functionality including joining calls, meetings, group chats, and channel messages are not impacted. Scenarios that depend on Exchange Online, including Calendar related failures with scheduling, invites, viewing, and meeting edits. Creation of Live or Virtual events fail. Failures with Copilot responses for outlook, calendar, or M365 files, read history, or adding to new chats. Navigating to App chats, adding new contacts or syncing contacts in settings fail. Standard channels are working fine but users may experience the inability to create or delete private or shared channels.
- Microsoft To Do: The app may not load, and users may see operation failures.
- Power BI: All users may intermittently be unable to export reports with MIP sensitivity labels to PDF in Power BI.
- SharePoint Online: Some users may experience issues when sharing SharePoint Online files with people outside their organization, where external sharing is permitted by both organization-level and site-level settings. Additionally, features that depend on Exchange Online may be impacted. Accessing files stored directly in SharePoint Online remains functional.
- Universal Print: Users may encounter errors submitting print jobs or using admin features.
- Windows 365: Customers who have configured their tenant and Cloud PCs to use Microsoft Purview Customer Key for Windows 365 Cloud PCs may have users who are unable to connect to their Cloud PCs.
Scope of impact: This issue may have affected users attempting to access the affected Microsoft 365 services.
Start time: Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 10:05 AM UTC
End time: Friday, November 13, 2026, at 4:10 PM UTC
Preliminary root cause: The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.
Next Steps: - For a more comprehensive list of next steps and actions, please refer to the Post Incident Report document that will be created for this event.
We'll provide a preliminary Post-Incident Report within two business days and a final Post-Incident Report within five business days.
Time:	Sat Nov 14 02:17:51 2026 UTC (Fri Nov 13 21:17:51 2026 EST)
Description:	Title: Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services
User impact: Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services.
Current status: We’ve confirmed continued recovery across previously affected environments. We’ll maintain monitoring to ensure the mitigation actions taken remain effective and track processing of the email backlog accumulated during the event.
We’re continuing to address any open impact scenarios across dependent and related Microsoft 365 products, as detailed in the ‘More info’ section below. We believe the majority of these scenarios have been addressed, with work continuing on any remaining scenarios.
More info: Features of the Microsoft 365 services below that interact with Exchange Online and email services are impacted. Elements of those services that do not depend on interaction with Exchange Online remain functional.
- Exchange Online: Users may be unable to access their mailbox using Outlook on the web, Outlook desktop (MAPI), Exchange ActiveSync (EAS), or REST-based connections, and email delivery may be delayed.

As a workaround, users can remove the sensitivity label from the affected item to complete the operation, if their organization's data protection policies allow it.
- Microsoft Graph: API requests that access Exchange Online data, such as mail, calendar, and contacts, may time out and prevent users from managing Teams, Channels, Membership, Apps management and send activity notifications using Graph API.

- Microsoft Power Apps: Users may be intermittently unable to sign-in to the Power Apps or Field Service mobile apps. Affected users may be able to utilize Power Apps or Field Service on the web as a way to circumvent impact, and users who are already signed in can potentially avoid impact by not signing out, clearing app data, or reinstalling while the issue is ongoing. Microsoft Power Apps and Microsoft Power Automate Flows, apps, data refreshes and connectors that rely on Microsoft Graph data were intermittently failing.

Audit searches, protected content creation, eDiscovery tasks such as search and export, Data Classification and On Demand Scan features may also be impacted.

Failures with Copilot responses for outlook, calendar, or M365 files, read history, or adding to new chats. Navigating to App chats, adding new contacts or syncing contacts in settings fail. Standard channels are working fine but users may experience the inability to create or delete private or shared channels.
- Microsoft To Do: The app may not load, and users may see operation failures.
- Power BI: All users may intermittently be unable to export reports with MIP sensitivity labels to PDF in Power BI.
- SharePoint Online: Some users may experience issues when sharing SharePoint Online files with people outside their organization, where external sharing is permitted by both organization-level and site-level settings. Additionally, features that depend on Exchange Online may be impacted. Accessing files stored directly in SharePoint Online remains functional.
- Universal Print: Users may encounter errors submitting print jobs or using admin features.
- Windows 365: Customers who have configured their tenant and Cloud PCs to use Microsoft Purview Customer Key for Windows 365 Cloud PCs may have users who are unable to connect to their Cloud PCs.
Scope of impact: This issue may affect users attempting to access the affected Microsoft 365 services.

CP1527498 - Some users may be unable to load chat history or previously pinned chats, and can't pin chats in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Status:	postIncidentReviewPublished
Start Time:	Tue Oct 27 15:58:45 2026 UTC (Tue Oct 27 11:58:45 2026 EDT)
End Time:	Wed Nov 4 16:08:21 2026 UTC (Wed Nov 4 11:08:21 2026 EST)
Service:	Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)
Feature Group:	Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)
Classification:	advisory
Last Updated:	Thu Nov 12 07:07:07 2026 UTC (Thu Nov 12 02:07:07 2026 EST)
Root Cause:	The pinned chats feature in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat contained a code defect that had been present since the feature was first released. This defect wasn’t caught during testing due to its difficulty to reproduce locally. A recent migration exposed this defect, which, under certain conditions, prevented pinned chats from loading and prevented users from pinning new chats.

CW1530567 - Users may be unable to view recent portions of their conversation history with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
Status:	postIncidentReviewPublished
Start Time:	Wed Oct 14 15:55:00 2026 UTC (Wed Oct 14 11:55:00 2026 EDT)
End Time:	Wed Nov 4 21:27:00 2026 UTC (Wed Nov 4 16:27:00 2026 EST)
Service:	Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
Feature Group:	Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
Classification:	incident
Last Updated:	Thu Nov 12 00:47:15 2026 UTC (Wed Nov 11 19:47:15 2026 EST)
Root Cause:	Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat keeps a cached copy of recent conversation activity so that history loads quickly when a user returns to a conversation. Each conversation is stored durably, and the cached copy is held in the part of our service infrastructure that handles the user's requests. During this event, two conditions combined so that some requests loaded an earlier cached copy of a conversation that didn't yet include its most recent exchanges. First, resource limitations in portions of the infrastructure supporting conversation history meant that some updates to the cached copy couldn't be completed in their usual location. Second, requests that load conversation history weren't always routed in the same way as requests that add new messages. As a result, a user returning to a conversation could sometimes be directed to a location holding an older copy of their history.
Next Update:	N/A
expand section Details

EX1478331 - Some users’ email messages may not be quarantined and fail to be stored in the quarantine folder
Status:	postIncidentReviewPublished
Start Time:	Wed Sep 23 00:56:00 2026 UTC (Tue Sep 22 20:56:00 2026 EDT)
End Time:	Fri Oct 2 08:24:00 2026 UTC (Fri Oct 2 04:24:00 2026 EDT)
Service:	Exchange Online
Feature Group:	E-Mail timely delivery
Classification:	incident
Last Updated:	Thu Nov 12 00:05:57 2026 UTC (Wed Nov 11 19:05:57 2026 EST)
Root Cause:	Exchange Online can place messages that match an organization's protection or data loss prevention (DLP) policies into quarantine, where administrators can review and release them. Some of these messages are stored in a quarantine location that belongs to the organization, and to route a message there, the service first identifies the organization it belongs to. A recent service update included a change to how our service creates and retrieves organization identity information. After this update, the step that routes messages to the organization's quarantine location was, in some cases, unable to obtain the organization's identifier. When this occurred, the service couldn't determine where to store the message, and the message was returned to the sender with the error "550 5.1.10 Failed to deliver to Quarantine store" instead of being quarantined.
Next Update:	N/A
expand section Details

Service:	SharePoint Online
Feature Group:	SharePoint Features
Classification:	incident
Last Updated:	Wed Oct 21 23:54:51 2026 UTC (Wed Oct 21 19:54:51 2026 EDT)
Root Cause:	SharePoint Online had been running a new version of the component that supplies page data alongside the existing one, and as part of a planned change that new version was promoted to become the primary one. It did not correctly handle two of the request patterns that custom forms rely on when a page loads, so requests for page data stopped partway through. Because the first part of the page had already been sent to the browser, the service was not able to replace it with an error message, which is why affected users saw a blank form rather than an explanation.
